description: Jinny Lee is a dedicated real estate professional in East Auckland, helping homeowners achieve premium results and guiding buyers to secure the right property with confidence. Backed by Ray White Botany, Jinny combines strong local knowledge, strategic marketing, and a client-first approach.
tone: warm yet confident, trustworthy, knowledgeable, approachable, community-focused, client-first

brand_positioning.jinny_role: trusted East Auckland real estate advisor
brand_positioning.differentiation: local market expertise, strong negotiation skills, personalised service

target_audience.secondary: buyers and families searching for homes in East Auckland
target_audience.entry_level: first-home buyers needing guidance and education

optimal_times: 08:00 — highest single-post engagement score in the Facebook insights period (engagement 3, image post, April 19); confirmed as a top-performing hour in facebook_insights.best_posting_hours; recommended for morning-scroll seller education content, listing reveals, and autumn urgency hooks targeting commuters and early risers in East Auckland; image posts at this hour produced the strongest available engagement signal in the data period and must be prioritised for the highest-value content of the week; this window has never been used across all 17 archived local posts which defaulted uniformly to 20:00 — correcting this scheduling omission is an immediate and overdue tactical priority that has now been recommended for three consecutive strategy periods without being actioned

10:00 — joint second-highest engagement score in the Facebook insights period (engagement 2, image posts, April 28 and April 13); confirmed in facebook_insights.best_posting_hours; recommended for mid-morning market update, buyer guidance, and suburb spotlight content when the East Auckland audience is actively browsing on mobile during a work break; image format confirmed as the top format at this hour; also absent from all 17 archived local posts; introducing mid-morning scheduling alongside morning posts will diversify reach across different audience browsing patterns during the peak weekday window

11:00 — newly confirmed top-performing hour in the Facebook insights period (engagement 2, image post, April 29); this is a new addition to the optimal posting schedule not present in the previous strategy and must be incorporated immediately as a third morning window option; confirmed in facebook_insights.best_posting_hours alongside 08:00 and 10:00; recommended for mid-morning property education, interest rate commentary, and local area content; provides flexibility for days where 08:00 or 10:00 scheduling is unavailable while remaining within the confirmed high-engagement morning window

20:00 to 21:00 — most common posting hour across all 17 archived local posts; retained as the primary evening window; 21:00 appeared in top-5 Facebook insight posts; recommended for seller education, community content, and interest rate commentary when East Auckland homeowners are in a relaxed end-of-day decision-making mindset; avoid making this the only posting window as the previous strategy did across all 17 archived posts — a split schedule combining morning windows at 08:00, 10:00, or 11:00 with the evening window is now the minimum recommended weekly scheduling approach to capture both morning-scroll and evening-browse audience segments
best_days: Tuesday through Thursday recommended as primary posting days for seller education, market update, and buyer guidance content based on general real estate social media best practices — low confidence due to insufficient day-level performance data in the current Facebook insights period; reassess when day-level engagement data becomes available in the next 30-day review cycle

Saturday morning at 08:00 to 10:00 recommended for listing reveals, open home announcements, and sold result posts to align with weekend buyer browsing and open home activity patterns in East Auckland — supported by 08:00 and 10:00 confirmed as top-performing hours in facebook_insights.best_posting_hours and consistent with general real estate audience behaviour on weekends in the New Zealand market

Sunday evening at 20:00 to 21:00 recommended for seller education and week-ahead market content targeting East Auckland homeowners in a relaxed end-of-weekend planning mindset — supported by the 21:00 performance signal from Facebook insights and the consistent 20:00 archive posting pattern; autumn urgency and interest rate hooks tied to the pre-winter window are the recommended content themes for this slot as urgency framing resonates strongly with homeowners in a reflective Sunday evening mindset
learned.image_to_text_ratio: 3:1 — minimum three image or video posts for every one text-only post per week; the current archive is 0:17 in favour of text across all recorded periods which is the complete inverse of recommended best practice per brand identity visual guidelines and all five research briefs; the three highest-engagement posts in the Facebook insights period were all image posts confirming visual formats outperform text even in a low-data environment; this ratio shift is the most urgent and most persistently unactioned tactical change in the strategy and must be implemented from the current week forward without exception or further deferral; compliance with this ratio should be audited weekly and any deviation must be escalated immediately
top_content_types: listing — hero interior and exterior shots showcasing lifestyle, indoor-outdoor flow, and premium East Auckland homes; confirmed as primary format based on brand identity guidelines and all three highest-engagement Facebook posts being image posts at 08:00, 11:00, and 10:00; low confidence due to zero reach and impression data; must be published at confirmed peak hours of 08:00, 10:00, or 11:00 to replicate the conditions of the top-performing posts; this format remains entirely absent from all 17 archived local posts and must be introduced immediately as a non-negotiable weekly content element

sold — celebration moments, sold sticker overlays, happy client handovers at front door with genuine emotion; social proof format cited across four of five research briefs as a direct trust-building driver of seller enquiries; entirely absent from all 17 archived local posts across three consecutive strategy periods making it the single highest-priority image type to introduce immediately; at least one sold story image post per week is recommended as a non-negotiable content element and must not be deferred again

lifestyle — family living moments, warm autumn-toned interiors, soft natural light through windows, indoor-outdoor connection; seasonal alignment with Autumn 2026 and early winter transition context confirmed across all five research briefs; autumn lifestyle framing remains the dominant seasonal visual tone and must be applied across all image post types through early May before the winter market slowdown arrives in June; as winter approaches in the second half of May, warm interior lifestyle imagery should transition toward cosy indoor living tones to maintain seasonal relevance

agent_brand — Jinny interacting with clients at open homes, behind-the-scenes of listing process, professional yet warm and approachable moments; transparency and personal brand content cited across multiple research briefs as a trust-building format during active market conditions; absent from all 17 archived local posts and recommended for introduction immediately to close the social proof and personality content gap; behind-the-scenes listing process walkthrough format specifically cited in two research briefs as building the trust needed to convert seller enquiries; this format must appear at least once per week

local_area — East Auckland streets, parks, school zones, suburban greenery, tree-lined streets, coastal lifestyle shots; suburb spotlight and school zone content noted across multiple research briefs as consistently building local authority and trust with family buyer audiences; currently absent from the archive; aligns with autumn school-term family research cycle making it timely and high-relevance now; multigenerational living demand flagged as a medium-relevance emerging trend across two briefs and East Auckland housing stock makes this a natural local authority angle to introduce this period
top_pillars: Seller Education — autumn selling season urgency and pre-winter listing timing remain at peak strategic relevance as confirmed across all five research briefs generated between April 15 and April 30 2026; seller education content tied to pricing strategy, home staging, listing preparation, the cost of waiting, and interest rate impacts on the East Auckland market should continue to lead the weekly content mix at 30 percent weighting through early May; the closing pre-winter window should be framed explicitly in content from this week forward as urgency is at its highest point and the June market slowdown is now less than four weeks away; interest rate cut angles must continue to be woven into seller education content as they are flagged as high-relevance across all five briefs and represent the strongest single evergreen hook for dual seller and buyer audiences

Trends and Short-form Content — short-form video under 30 seconds is flagged as the highest watch-through format in April 2026 across multiple research briefs and has never appeared in the 17-post archive across any recorded strategy period; introducing at least one TikTok or Instagram Reel per week is now the most urgent single format gap to close and cannot be deferred for a fourth consecutive period; behind-the-scenes listing process walkthroughs, one-thing-sellers-always-forget formats, open home day preparation, and quick property tip videos are the recommended entry formats; algorithm momentum on video-first platforms depends on consistency beginning immediately

Listings and Success Stories — sold results and client success case studies cited across four of five research briefs as social proof drivers of seller enquiries; this format is entirely absent from all 17 archived local posts across three consecutive strategy periods and represents the most significant and longest-running missed trust-conversion opportunity in the archive; at least one sold story or case study image post per week is a non-negotiable content element that must be introduced this week without further deferral; this format directly converts social browsing sellers into enquiry contacts and its absence for three consecutive periods is a measurable missed opportunity during the busiest selling season of the year

Personal Brand and Trust — behind-the-scenes listing content and transparency posts cited across multiple research briefs as trust-building during active market conditions; Jinny's personal brand presence is entirely absent from all 17 archived local posts and must appear at least once per week from this point forward; open home walk-in moments, client interaction shots, and listing preparation behind-the-scenes content are the recommended entry formats; personal brand content is a direct differentiator from generic competitor agent content and builds the know-like-trust progression required to convert a social follower into a seller enquiry

voice_guide.headline_style: short punchy, 2–6 words, benefit-driven or curiosity-based
voice_guide.caption_style: hook first, value or story, then soft CTA — no hashtags in body
